prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by bifunctional degraders that direct ubiquitin ligases to chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is the one candidate that nearly the whole committee ranks highly (seven of eight in the top three), and my own opening placed it second only because I was drawn to Car-Parrinello as a method I know well. On reflection it is the stronger prize. The central idea is chemical in the most literal sense: a rationally designed heterobifunctional small molecule that brings a ubiquitin ligase and a target together so the target is destroyed. Event-driven, catalytic pharmacology replaces occupancy-based inhibition, and this opens targets once thought undruggable. The concept dates to Crews and Deshaies in 2001, and Ciulli's structure-based VHL ligands and ternary-complex work turned it into a design discipline that can be taught and generalised. Independent validation is extensive, with many clinical candidates, and this is a change in how drugs are conceived.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved yet, so some of the case rests on clinical promise rather than outcome. Attribution is also genuinely hard. The molecular-glue and cereblon strand (Handa, Ito, and the thalidomide history) and the later chemoproteomic and glue-discovery work (Gray and others) are a distinct lineage, and a three-person limit forces us to choose a single story. A citation that credits only PROTACs may look unfair to the glue community, while a broad citation risks blurring the chemistry. If the committee judges the clinical evidence too immature, B061 is the better prize in a mature field.

responses.point: Linke ranks degraders first and proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa, so that cereblon, the target of thalidomide, is credited along with the PROTAC concept.
responses.response: I agree on the ranking but not on replacing Ciulli with Handa. Handa's identification of cereblon is a real discovery, but it explains a mechanism of drugs found empirically, while Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are the chemistry that made rational degrader design possible. A citation built on designed degraders fits Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli better. If the committee wants the glue strand in the prize, I would accept Handa in place of Deshaies only with a citation that explicitly covers both modalities, and I am not convinced yet.

responses.point: Brzezinski places nitrogenase first for its structurally and mechanistically well-defined chemistry, and he has degraders second, with Handa among the laureates.
responses.response: I share his preference for a chemically concrete prize, and the nitrogenase structure and cofactor work is excellent. My concern is the same one I see in the attribution: five people (Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean, Ribbe) share the credit, the mechanism of substrate reduction is still being refined, and only he ranks it. I cannot raise it above degraders without broader support, but I would like to hear his answer on whether the unresolved mechanism affects maturity.

responses.point: Chabes puts base editing first as a clearly defined chemical tool, with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as laureates.
responses.response: I rate base editing highly, and it is my third choice. I would still not give it the top place. Liu is clearly the decisive figure, and Komor and Gaudelli were trainees, which makes a Liu-only prize the cleaner option, and I do not follow Chabes in naming two trainees. It also follows the 2020 genome-editing prize closely, and the clinical record is much shorter than for degraders. It is a strong choice for a later year.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling first because the chemistry is mature and cleanly attributed and its industrial impact is enormous.
responses.response: The attribution is the cleanest on our list and the impact is undeniable, so I agree on both points and keep it in my top five. My reservation is that a prize would largely continue the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and I would rather reward a new conceptual step now. If the committee prefers a safe, mature synthetic prize, I would support it, but I would not rank it above degraders.

responses.point: Aili ranks degraders first on conceptual novelty and puts lipid nanoparticles second, noting the glue lineage may need separate recognition.
responses.response: I agree with the conceptual argument and with his point that the glue lineage is the main open question. I am less certain about lipid nanoparticles. The impact is very large, but credit is spread among Cullis, Anderson, Langer, MacLachlan, Hope and Madden, and the mRNA vaccine side was recognised in Medicine 2023, so I would keep it behind degraders.

uncertainties: Whether the glue and cereblon lineage (Handa, Ito, Gray) can be credited alongside PROTACs within the three-person limit, and with what citation.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader drug makes a 2026 award premature compared with a mature prize such as B061.
Whether I have the detailed priority and dates for the 2001 PROTAC paper and the VHL ligand work right, since I am relying on memory.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B020, B047, B044 or B028. For B061 (Car-Parrinello), my work is in biomolecular simulation, but my profile does not identify any personal tie to Car or Parrinello. My connection to Arieh Warshel (a postdoc collaboration on EVB) is not relevant to any shortlisted ballot.
